rationales: Vacuoles are membrane-bound storage compartments, not the intended cisternae.
Mitochondria have internal cristae rather than the cisternae referred to here.
The Golgi apparatus consists of flattened membrane-bound cisternae.
The nucleus is not described as a stack of cisternae in this context.
Aluminium is not generally classified as a bioelement in this context.
Cobalt is a trace element but is not the intended answer among these choices.
Bromine is not generally classified as a bioelement in this context.
Carbon is a major bioelement found in living organisms.
Cell biology studies cells, not specifically insects.
Entomology is the branch of biology that studies insects.
Morphology studies the form and structure of organisms.
Taxonomy deals with naming and classifying organisms.
Epithelial tissue includes glandular epithelium, which forms glands.
Muscular tissue is specialized for contraction, not gland secretion.
Connective tissue supports and connects body structures rather than forming glands.
Nervous tissue conducts signals rather than forming glands.
Whittaker did not introduce the five-kingdom system in 1896.
Whittaker did not introduce the five-kingdom system in 1976.
Whittaker did not introduce the five-kingdom system in 1866.
Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom system in 1969, so 1967 is incorrect.
Observations are recorded findings, not the logical consequences derived from a hypothesis.
A deduction is a logical consequence derived from a hypothesis.
Experiments test a hypothesis or its predictions rather than name the logical consequences.
A theory is a broad explanation supported by evidence, not a prediction from a hypothesis.
An ecosystem includes organisms and their interactions with the environment, not just Earth's inhabited part.
A habitat is the place where a particular organism or population lives.
The biosphere is the part of Earth inhabited by living organisms.
A population consists of members of one species living in an area.
Mitochondria are not primarily responsible for lipid storage.
Mitochondria are the main site of cellular respiration and ATP production.
Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts, not mitochondria.
Protein synthesis occurs at ribosomes, not as the mitochondrion's main function.
C₆H₁₂O₆ is the formula for glucose, not lactic acid.
C₆H₂₂O₁₁ is not the formula for lactic acid.
C₂H₂OH is not the correct molecular formula for lactic acid.
Lactic acid has the molecular formula C₃H₆O₃.
27°C is below the optimum temperature for most human enzymes.
About 37°C is the optimum temperature for most human enzymes.
50°C is high enough to denature many human enzymes.
100°C would denature human enzymes.
Prophase is one stage of mitosis and lasts far less time than interphase.
Metaphase is a brief stage of mitosis.
Cells spend most of the cell cycle in interphase.
Telophase is a brief final stage of mitosis.
Acetyl CoA combines with oxaloacetate to enter the Krebs cycle.
Citric acid is formed within the Krebs cycle rather than being the usual entry substrate.
Pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl CoA before entering the Krebs cycle.
Glucose is broken down through glycolysis before its products enter the Krebs cycle.
The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
The left atrium contains oxygenated blood returning from the lungs.
The left ventricle contains oxygenated blood that is pumped to the body.
Digestion breaks large food molecules into smaller, absorbable molecules.
Absorption is the movement of digested nutrients into the blood or lymph.
Assimilation converts absorbed nutrients into complex substances used by the body.
Ingestion is the taking of food into the body.
The stomach temporarily holds food during digestion, not faeces.
The gall bladder stores bile, not faeces.
The urinary bladder stores urine, not faeces.
The rectum temporarily stores faeces before defecation.
